tier_reason: The benchmark_url (repo) has no numbers and its speedtest.h only times SPIDER itself; the peer-reviewed SEA 2024 paper (LIPIcs.SEA.2024.21, arXiv 2405.05214) is the real evidence but Dagstuhl, arXiv and review sites are egress-blocked, so its claims were seen only as WebSearch snippets. Snippet-only numbers cap at C until a paper-access retier can confirm B.

corrections.baseline: pasta-flat and pasta-wide, poppy (cs-poppy), Vigna's rank9 and SDSL rank/select structures (competitor list from WebSearch snippets of the SEA 2024 paper; paper not opened)
corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippets of the SEA 2024 paper / arXiv 2405.05214 (snippet only, paper blocked): 3.82-3.83% space overhead; 'the fastest known structure for bit vectors of 8 billion bits or more, outperforming pasta-flat by 22%' for rank; for select it improves on the state of the art with under 5% extra space and 'nearly matches' the best known succinct structure that uses 12.5% space (i.e. not faster than that one). No per-baseline ratio against SDSL seen.
corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed at SEA 2024 (LIPIcs vol. 301, paper 21), but the paper (Dagstuhl, arXiv) is blocked here, so the claim text is from WebSearch snippets only (snippet only); tier B is likely once the paper can be read. The repo README has no benchmark numbers, flags or CPU, and no LICENSE file exists (LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, COPYING all 404; no license header in spider.c), so code must not be copied. Code is x86-only (includes x86intrin.h; Makefile builds with gcc -O9 -march=native -mpopcnt -mlzcnt). Rank benefit is reported for very large vectors (8 billion bits or more); select is close to, not faster than, the best 12.5%-space structure.

notes: Repo exists (5 stars, 1 fork, 10 commits, last commit 2024-05-28 'minor fix', no license); metadata in the record is correct. Downgraded B to C only because the paper could not be opened; queue a paper-access retier (Dagstuhl PDF LIPIcs.SEA.2024.21.pdf) to restore B.

tier_reason: README and the companion paper PDF checked into the repo (succint_bitvec.pdf) give first-party Google Benchmark numbers against SDSL rank_support_v and select_support_mcl, with public bench code (src/bench.cpp, BM_Rank_SDSL under HAS_SDSL), Apple Clang 15.0.0 and -O3 -march=native -std=c++17 -DNDEBUG; the CPU is only 'Apple Silicon M-series', so not A, and the paper is an unreviewed single-author preprint, so not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table at N=1M, 50% density: FastBitVec rank 1.65 ns vs SDSL rank_support_v 2.25 ns (about 1.36x, derived from page data); FastBitVec select 44.5 ns vs SDSL select_support_mcl 78.4 ns (about 1.76x, derived from page data); RRRBitVec select 33.7 ns (paper states 2.33x over SDSL). Paper Table 1 rank across sizes: FastBitVec 1.65/1.65/1.71/1.95 ns vs SDSL 2.32/2.25/2.29/2.45 ns at 100K/1M/10M/100M (about 1.26x at 100M, derived from page data). Total space 1.141 bpe vs SDSL 1.250 bpe (SDSL figure counts only the rank_support_v directory; select_support_mcl adds more).
corrections.caveats: Single-author preprint (companion PDF succint_bitvec.pdf is in the repo; the arXiv number 2605.25528 does not appear in the README or the PDF, so it is unverified here), not peer reviewed. The headline README table is N=1M (cache-resident); the paper's Table 1 extends rank to 100M (12.5 MB, beyond the 4 MiB L2), where the FastBitVec lead narrows to about 1.26x (derived from page data); select is only reported at 1M. Exact CPU model missing ('Apple Silicon M-series, 64 KiB L1D, 4 MiB L2'), so tier C not A. SDSL rank_support_v is not the most compact SDSL rank (v5 has less space), and sux, pasta, poppy and SPIDER were not compared. The SDSL space figure excludes the select_support_mcl directory. Correctness fuzzer with 78M assertions is included. README's clone URL points to github.com/ishgarg/succinct-bitvec-cpp, not this repo.
